speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip to Minnesota and the migrating joint pain, I suspect Lyme disease. Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions, and have you noticed any tick bites or a bull's-eye rash?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists, combined with fever and monoarticular arthritis, strongly suggests Erythema Chronicum Migrans is not the cause, but rather a different spirochetal infection like Relapsing Fever or perhaps secondary syphilis, though the lesion description is classic for something else. I need to rule out specific infections common in camping scenarios or sexually transmitted diseases.

Do you have a headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light? Also, have you had any recent sexual encounters without protection, and can you confirm if the lesions appeared after the camping trip or before?
